budget.rationale: The six categories reconcile exactly to $10,700–$14,800, but the two-stop Ljubljana airfare and 2027 lodging remain planning proxies. With medium-confidence evidence and a high case within $200 of the preferred maximum, the rubric caps Budget at 2/5 until the full family quote is confirmed.

weather.rationale: A genuine split: the Piran coast is warm and mostly dry in June (~25–28°C), but the Julian Alps see frequent June afternoon thunderstorms and the Vršič Pass carries a real late-snow timing risk. The gorges and caves are the smart rainy-window picks, so the score reflects manageable-but-recurring mountain weather exposure.

fireRisk.rationale: Low is the safety rating (4/5), corresponding to a 2–5% planning chance of material wildfire disruption during the exact trip window. The moist alpine half is low risk; the Karst and coastal southwest can burn. EFFIS mapped only two Slovenian fires in 2024, while the July 2024 Karst fire demonstrates that localized disruption is credible later in summer.

swim.rationale: The Piran Adriatic is a swimmable ~22°C / 72°F in June — warmer and calmer than the Atlantic plans but cooler than the Greek/Crete lagoons, off rocky platforms rather than warm sand. The glacial Soča and Alpine lakes are look-and-raft, not swim. Usable, limited, and refreshing water scores 3; Croatia, the obvious warm partner, is excluded by family decision.

variety.rationale: Alpine lakes, an emerald river, three gorges, a UNESCO cave, a mountain pass, a Venetian coast, and a capital city across one compact country is the full spread of water, towns, and nature.

ease.rationale: On the ground this is one of the easiest plans on the board: one country, one rental car, four bases in a tidy loop, short drives, no intra-Europe flight and no open-jaw. It scores 3 rather than higher only because Ljubljana has no long-haul service, so the air routing is a two-stop itinerary with a fragile final leg.

food.rationale: Every base (Bled, Bohinj, Bovec, Piran, Ljubljana) has full supermarkets (Mercator/Spar) plus reliable wood-fired pizza, pasta, and burgers — strong picky-eater coverage. It is inexpensive, but cost is scored under budget, not food.

risk.rationale: Exact protected PIT–LJU inventory is selling. The remaining uncertainty is the Vršič Pass and ordinary road/weather disruption, supporting Risk 4/5.

nights.rationale: Twelve hotel nights derive 5/5 under the canonical nights rubric.

novelty.rationale: Slovenia does not overlap the documented visited-place list, and the Julian Alps and Karst caves are unlike anything else on the board, deriving 5/5.

pto.rationale: Eight PTO days derive 3/5 under the slider rubric and have zero default weight; Juneteenth observed (Fri Jun 18) is used as a no-PTO active day.
